title: Expected issue list
description: Derived from design/EVALUATION_INTERFACES.md 1.2 (Draft); the document wins. Proposal: Tillman Heisner accepts, changes or replaces it (Evaluation interfaces, section 4). Every issue the deterministic verifier should raise in round 1 for one item (section 4.3), as (kind, pointer or set of pointers), scored by exact match. Mode A only: the file carries mode A (section 4.1 rule 12), because mode B does not score the deterministic verifier (section 2.2).
$comment: Derived from design/EVALUATION_INTERFACES.md 1.2 (Draft); the document wins. Section 4.1 rule 4 leaves the file format (CSV, JSON or another) to the builder; this file describes the JSON form, with one object per row in rows. Key names that section 4 does not give are marked 'Proposed name' in their description. Rows follow the grouping convention of 4.3: one issue per pointer, except OR-rule issues; missing issues at the highest empty level. rule_id and note are for reading only, not for matching. Kinds follow Issue format 0.6, 4.1 (the kinds the deterministic verifier raises). Section 4.1 rule 12 gives the three mode-keyed expected files a required mode, A or B; for this file section 4.3 and section 10.8 allow A only, so its rows are always keyed by kind and pointers, matched as in 4.1 rule 8.

item_id.description: The item the file is for (4.1 rule 1).

variant_id.description: The variant the file is for (4.1 rule 1).

input_files.description: Proposed name. The input-side files the expected file was built for, each with its SHA-256 (4.1 rule 1). If a checksum no longer matches, the scorer skips the item and reports it.

evaluation_interfaces_version.description: Proposed name. The version of design/EVALUATION_INTERFACES.md the file follows (4.1 rule 1).

expected_file_version.description: Proposed name. The version of this expected file; a reviewed finding goes into a new version, and scores name it (4.1 rule 5).

issue_format_version.description: The issue-format version the expected issues follow (4.1 rule 1; 4.3), for example 0.6. Key name as in design/HANDOFFS.md 2.7.

mode.description: The evaluation mode whose keys the rows use (section 4.1 rule 12): always A here, rows keyed by kind and pointers; mode B does not score the deterministic verifier (sections 2.2 and 4.3).

canary.description: Only if canaries are adopted (5.3): the file's canary, random and at least 32 characters long. Option CS7, a canary in every row, would add a row field.

pointer.description: A JSON Pointer into the EnzymeML document, for example /measurements/0/ph (Issue format 2). For software only; scientists never see pointers.

sha256.description: A SHA-256 checksum: 64 hexadecimal characters, computed by software (Evaluation interfaces 3.1).

input_file.description: One input-side file the expected file was built for, with its checksum (4.1 rule 1). Field names from Evaluation interfaces 3.1.

kind.description: An issue kind the deterministic verifier raises (Issue format 4.1).

fields.description: Proposed name, after the issue field it is matched with. The pointer or set of pointers (Issue format 4, fields).

rule_id.description: Optional, for reading only (Issue format 4 and 8).

note.description: Proposed name. Optional short note, for reading only.

pending.description: Proposed name. true for a row not yet settled: left out of scores and listed (4.1 rule 3). Frozen test-set files hold no pending rows.

examples.note: The draft has no creators; one issue at the highest empty level.
The substrate is given only as a range.

rows.note: The substrate is given only as a range.
